reconstructed_theorem_text: For every real number δ satisfying 0 < δ < 1, there exists a natural number d₀ such that the following holds. For every natural number d with d₀ ≤ d, every real number κ satisfying 2 ≤ κ and κ ≤ (d : ℝ)^(1 − δ), and every natural number q satisfying (q : ℝ) ≤ (δ / 256) · sqrt(κ) · log(d : ℝ), define the natural number n to be exactly 2q + 1. Then all four assertions hold: 2 ≤ d, 1 ≤ n, n < d, and sqrt(κ) ≤ (d : ℝ) − (n : ℝ). The first three conclusions are inequalities in the natural numbers, and the final inequality is in the real numbers. The threshold d₀ is chosen after δ and its two strict-inequality hypotheses and before d, κ, or q; it therefore cannot depend on d, κ, or q. Here q and d may range over all natural numbers, including zero, subject only to the displayed hypotheses; n is the stated local definition, not a separately quantified or existentially chosen value. The expression 1 − δ is real subtraction and is the real exponent in the power. The final difference is real subtraction of the two casts, not a cast of natural-number subtraction. The expression 2q + 1 is computed in the natural numbers. The coefficient δ / 256 and the factors sqrt(κ) and log(d : ℝ) are real-valued; multiplication has the displayed product meaning. Logarithm, square root, and real power retain their stated standard totalized real-function meanings, without additional domain hypotheses. The δ endpoints are excluded; the d threshold, both κ bounds, the q bound, the first two concluding bounds, and the concluding real bound are inclusive; n < d is strict.
